items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: And Chou En-lai, who studied in the west, studied in Paris, was friends with W.E.B. Debois, and was jazz was played he was dancing.

ctx.x: Because well we see Min Xiao-Fen is performing with me on pipa. And when Chinese come over here there’s that social interaction, the musical interaction, and then they become sort of the modern Chinese-born American. Whereas, and you could see, well I’ll give you an example of two great leaders: Mao Tse Tung, okay? So there’s a story about one of the Chinese saxophonists who was older than me by about twenty years, who performed for Mao. And Chou En-lai, who studied in the west, studied in Paris, was friends with…

Well last week, timely, there was a couple of Chinese students. I’m not even sure they were teaching assistants, they did an hour program on Chinese popular music. One did something she called Chinese rock & roll. And the other one did, and I wish I had written the word down, there was a term that apparently there’s a popular style that combines almost hip hop, that kind of thing, using traditional Chinese instruments. It was very interesting. And it’s amazing how pervasive Western pop music is now around the…
